title: Artifact shepherding: staged rollout and rollback contract
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview
This document defines the artifact shepherding contract for staged rollouts and rollbacks on Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It formalizes the signals, gating thresholds, operator procedures, and evidence-retention requirements that must be satisfied for a model or runtime artifact to progress through canary -> ramp -> full release, and the exact steps to safely rollback. It applies to control-plane and data-plane artifacts (serving runtime binaries, model bundles, quantized weights, kernel patches, operator images).

Scope
- Applies to all private-deploy customer environments managed by Redwood (VPC and on-prem packaged installs).
- Covers: artifact signing & provenance, preflight validation, canary orchestration, automated and manual rollback triggers, post-rollback forensic evidence collection.
- Excludes: customer-managed model training pipelines and customer-owned third-party appliances (see related_pages for handoff guidance).

Goals
- Minimize customer-facing impact during upgrades.
- Ensure deterministic rollback that preserves customer state and audit evidence.
- Provide clear, reproducible operator playbook for on-call and field engineers.

Key roles and ownership
- Release Owner (engineering): owns stage gating, artifact bundles, and the rollout schedule.
- Field Operator (operator / customer engineering): executes rollout and rollback in the customer environment and performs local verification.
- SRE Oncall: monitors platform-level SLOs and authorizes emergency rollback if automated circuits do not trigger.
- Security/Compliance Reviewer: verifies artifact provenance (signatures, SBOM) for regulated customers before ramp.

Prerequisites (pre-release checklist)
1. Artifact packaging: each bundle must include a signed manifest (COSE/PKCS7) and SBOM. The manifest contains: semantic_version, checksums (sha256), compatible_runtime_ids, and rollback_guard_tags.
2. Operator tools: field environment must have redwoodctl >= 1.12.0 installed, with operator credentials and a valid operator-session token.
3. Telemetry contract: customer telemetry export must include these metrics at 30s resolution: request_per_sec, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tok_per_request, model_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate.
4. Backup: snapshot of KV cache and stateful operator artifacts taken and stored off-host. Snapshot command: redwoodctl snapshot create --name pre-release-<artifact>-YYYYMMDD.

Staged rollout strategy (canonical flow)
1) Canary (0 -> 2%):
   - Deploy artifact to a small canary cohort (2% traffic or 1 small tenant, whichever is more conservative).
   - Retain both old and new model weights and the ability to route by tenant.
   - Minimum dwell time: 30 minutes or 10k requests, whichever is reached first.
   - Automatic gating checks (see gating criteria) run continuously.
2) Ramp (2% -> 25%):
   - Increase traffic in timed increments: 2% -> 10% -> 25% over 2 hours, pausing 20 minutes at each step to validate.
   - At each pause, run the full validation suite: synthetic traces, baseline eval prompts, and production smoke queries as described in Validation section.
3) Broad roll (25% -> 100%):
   - Continue to 50% then 100% only after passing two consecutive ramp windows with green signals and signoff from Release Owner.

Gating criteria (automated triggers)
- Abort and immediate rollback if any of the following are observed during a dwell window: 
  - Absolute error-rate increase: model_error_rate increases by >0.5 percentage points and the delta is statistically significant with p<0.01 over the last 30 minutes.
  - Latency degradation: p95_latency_ms increases by >50% or exceeds 500ms sustained for 10 minutes.
  - Token budget regressions: tok_per_request increases >25% without commensurate quality improvement (see quality checks).
  - KV cache regressions: kv_cache_hit_rate drops by >15% leading to >10% increase in back-end load.
  - Resource saturation: GPU utilization >95% on primary nodes for >5 minutes.
- Soft warning thresholds: p50 latency increase >20%, error-rate increase >0.2pp — these notify SRE and Release Owner and pause automatic ramps pending review.

Manual rollback criteria (operator discretion)
- Single-customer severe error (data corruption, PII exposure), or customer SLA breach.
- Failed dependency rollout (e.g., operator CRD changed and was not applied correctly).
- Security or compliance compromise detected in SBOM or signature validation.

Rollback procedures (ordered checklist)
1. Initiate rollback command (preferred automated path if gated):
   - redwoodctl rollout rollback --target <deployment-id> --to-version <previous-semver> --preserve-snapshots
2. If automated rollback fails or is unavailable, perform explicit operator fallback:
   - Step A: Quiesce incoming traffic to the affected tenant cohort: redwoodctl traffic set-weights --deployment <id> --weights old:100,new:0
   - Step B: Restore model artifact and runtime image from signed archive: redwoodctl image install --from s3://redwood-artifacts/<artifact>-vX.Y.Z --verify-signature
   - Step C: Apply operator manifest rollback: kubectl -n redwood operator set image redwood-operator=redwood/operator:<previous-tag>
   - Step D: Rehydrate state from snapshot if required: redwoodctl snapshot restore --name pre-release-<artifact>-YYYYMMDD --target <deployment-id>
3. Post-rollback verification (must complete before closing incident):
   - Verify all gating metrics are within pre-release baseline for 60 minutes.
   - Run smoke test suite (listed in Validation).
   - Confirm no loss of persistent requests and that KV cache coherence is restored.
4. Evidence capture: collect operator logs, artifact manifests, signature verification output, and telemetry windows for the entire rollout and rollback period. Store in the evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/<customer-id>/<artifact>-YYYYMMDD/. Preserve for minimum 90 days for regulated customers.

Validation and acceptance tests (examples)
- Baseline eval prompts: 200 prompt set used to compare semantic deviation. Pass criteria: mean semantic-similarity drop <0.02 measured with the approved comparator model.
- Synthetic throughput run: 30-minute steady-state at 1.5x expected QPS with 95th percentile latency < configured SLO.
- End-to-end trace checks: sampled requests must show no >2% increase in external service calls (upstream indices, database) attributable to artifact change.

Telemetry and monitoring contract
- Required dashboards: "Artifact Rollout Overview", "Canary Health Summary", "KV Cache Drift", and "Model Quality Regression".
- Alerting: automated must-fail alerts for gating criteria must notify SRE, Field Operator, and Release Owner via the oncall channel and create a paging incident if severity is P1.
- Sampling: preserve full traces for 2 hours, aggregated metrics for 30 days, and raw request logs for 7 days by default. For customers with compliance needs, extend to 365 days as per their telemetry SLA.

Forensic and audit tasks after rollback
- Freeze related telemetry windows for the duration of the investigation.
- Generate artifact provenance report: include manifest signatures, uploader identity, and SBOM diff between versions.
- If data exposure is suspected, follow the private-deploy evidence-preservation playbook (see related_pages).

Post-release remediation and learnings
- Required deliverables within 72 hours of rollback: a short incident brief (what changed, why gate failed, immediate fixes), and a remediation plan with owner and ETA.
- Release Owner must create a follow-up action ticket for any required runtime or model quantization adjustments.
- If rollback was triggered by quality regression, add failing prompts to the guarded prompt set and schedule a regression evaluation in the next model onboarding sprint.

Appendix A — Example gating table (human-readable)
Rows: Metric | Baseline | Abort delta | Soft warning
- model_error_rate | 0.6% | +0.5pp (abort) | +0.2pp (warn)
- p95_latency_ms | 180ms | +50% or >500ms (abort) | +20% (warn)
- kv_cache_hit_rate | 72% | -15pp (abort) | -8pp (warn)
- gpu_util | 65% | >95% sustained 5m (abort) | 80% (warn)

Appendix B — Quick CLI cheatsheet
- Create snapshot: redwoodctl snapshot create --name pre-release-<artifact>-$(date +%F)
- Start canary: redwoodctl rollout start --deployment <id> --artifact <artifact-uri> --stage canary --canary-percent 2
- Check rollout status: redwoodctl rollout status --deployment <id>
- Force rollback: redwoodctl rollout rollback --deployment <id> --to-version <previous-semver>

Appendix C — Escalation matrix
- 0–15 minutes: Field Operator triages and attempts automated rollback.
- 15–60 minutes: SRE oncall engaged; Release Owner notified.
- >60 minutes or data-loss event: Executive on-call and Security engaged, customer CS lead notified.

References and related pages
- See related_pages for the forensic rollback protocol and operator handshake runbooks.
- SBOM and signature guidelines: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/artifact-signing-guidelines (internal link).
